newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters rejects claims he's captured by NZ Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Peters rejects claims he's captured by NZ Treasury.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters on Wednesday rejected opposition claims that he had been captured by his department, and maintained he had held a consistent policy line.
On Tuesday, Peters said he would not react to "short term crises" in the exchange rate and would let the market respond as it saw fit.
During the election campaign Peters argued that the exchange rate for the New Zealand dollar was too high and was hurting exporters.

"In the space of a few short weeks the Treasurer has been completely captured by Treasury...the Treasurer has reinvented himself as market darling and Treasury poodle," Labour's finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Tuesday.
But Peters told National Radio on Wednesday opposition politicians were bitter about not getting into government and would continue to criticise him.
"We're going to have to grin and bear all that and get on with running the country. None of that is true," he said.
Peters suggested his opponents should carefully read the speech he made yesterday to business leaders because it showed the differences between National and New Zealand First.
"My line is consistent in the current circumstances," he said.
"What these people are suggesting is that by some political statement they can change everything. They simply cannot.
"What there needs to be is an understanding that much of the long term improvement of this country is down to business people and ordinary New Zealanders."
